places.name: Bonham State Park
places.coord_point: park contact block (1363 State Park 24, Bonham TX 75418)
places.blurb: A 65-acre lake with tent sites that have water and electricity, full-hookup sites and a group barracks, northeast of Dallas.
places.status_note: Official page says reservations are highly recommended for camping and day use. Active alerts are linked (alert text not read).
places.notes: NAME CANDIDATES (ten, batch 11): Ephemeris (chosen), Azimuth, Quadrant, Lodestar, Plumbline, Culmen, Starwheel, Tallybook, Hinge, Almucantar. Coordinates are printed on the official page in its contact block (Latitude 33.546727, Longitude -96.144758), rounded to 5 decimals. Wikipedia infobox point 33.54472, -96.14556 is about 220 m away, so the official point was used. A separate lat/lon pair appears only inside a National Weather Service forecast URL on the page and was not used. County Fannin is from the Wikipedia infobox (the official page does not state one). Acreage 261 is the Wikipedia total area; the official page gives only a 65-acre lake. Camping: official page lists tent sites with water and electricity, full hookups, a six-site group camp and a 94-person group barracks. Wikipedia also mentions water-only sites, which is not a coded kind. No dispersed, primitive, cabin or lodge camping on the page. Dark Sky: not on the TPWD dark skies page and not stated by Wikipedia. Phone for reservations (512) 389-8900. Nearby names are the ones the official page and Wikipedia name; distances not checked.

places.name: Davis Mountains State Park
places.coord_point: park location block (TX-118 N., Park Rd. 3, Fort Davis TX 79734)
places.blurb: Mountain state park above Fort Davis with a historic lodge, six primitive sites and six equestrian sites.
places.status_note: No closure or day-use-only notice on the page. Reservations advised, not required. Alerts are shown (a screwworm alert and a park alert page); their text was not read.
places.notes: Official page location block prints Latitude 30.599103 and Longitude -103.929450. Wikipedia infobox point 30.59583, -103.93278 is about 500 m away and was not used. The National Weather Service URL coordinates on the page were not used. County Jeff Davis and acreage 2,709 are from the Wikipedia infobox (the official page prints neither). The page's camping list names primitive sites in Limpia Canyon, equestrian sites and Indian Lodge (a 39-room historic motel); it does not mention tent or RV sites. Wikipedia says campground facilities were added in 1967 without naming types. The /stay page returned 404, so tent or RV camping is unconfirmed and not coded. Dark Sky: the page mentions stargazing but no designation, and the TPWD dark skies page does not list it. Trade-off: the nearby list uses names the official page gives; distances not checked.

places.name: Franklin Mountains State Park
places.coord_point: headquarters details on official page (Tom Mays Unit, 2900 Tom Mays Access Rd, El Paso TX 79911)
nearby: Hueco Tanks State Park & Historic Site
places.blurb: Desert mountain park on the north edge of El Paso with 14 walk-in tent sites and group camps.
places.status_note: No closure or day-use-only notice. Reservations recommended for camping and day use, not required. Alerts are shown; their text was not read.
places.notes: COORDINATE DISAGREEMENT: the official page's headquarters point (31.910522, -106.518182) and the Wikipedia infobox point (31.88361, -106.50222) are about 3.4 km apart, over the 2 km limit. The official point was used and this disagreement is recorded. Acreage: the official page says almost 27,000 acres; the Wikipedia infobox says 24,247. The exact Wikipedia figure is used here; the official rounded figure is not coded. County: El Paso, taken from the Wikipedia category tag (Protected areas of El Paso County); no county line appears in the infobox or the official page. Camping: the official page says 14 walk-in tent sites and five RV sites with no water or electricity. No RV kind is coded because no matching kind exists for unserviced RV sites. Group camps can be rented. Dark Sky: not on the TPWD dark skies page and not stated by Wikipedia. Nearby names are the ones the official page gives; distances not checked.

places.name: Kickapoo Cavern State Park
places.coord_point: park location block (20939 RR 674, Brackettville TX 78832)
nearby: Seminole Canyon State Park & Historic Site
places.blurb: Guided show caves and a park on the Edwards Plateau edge, with full-hookup sites and water-only campsites.
places.status_note: The headquarters hours on the official page list Park Closed Tuesday through Thursday; confirm before a trip. Guided cave tours require reservations. The page advises reserving ahead because the park often reaches capacity. Alerts are shown (including a screwworm alert); the text was not read.
places.notes: Official page location block prints Latitude 29.610016 and Longitude -100.452465. The Wikipedia infobox point 29.61194, -100.44833 is about 450 m away and was not used. County: the Wikipedia infobox lists both Edwards and Kinney; the official address is Brackettville, the Kinney County seat, so Kinney is coded. Acreage 6,368 is from Wikipedia. Camping per the official page: five full-hookup sites, ten water-only sites (not a coded kind), a 30-person group camp, and no RVs over 36 feet. No tent sites are named on the page, so tent is not coded. The official page names Devil's Sinkhole, Garner, Devils River, Seminole Canyon, Lost Maples and South Llano River as nearby; the three listed here are the closest of those by my reading, but their distances from this park were NOT checked against a map.

places.name: Lockhart State Park
places.coord_point: park contact block (2012 State Park Road, Lockhart TX 78644)
places.blurb: Creekside park with water-and-electric and full-hookup campsites under tall trees, plus a group recreation hall.
places.status_note: No closure or day-use-only notice. Reservations recommended for camping and day use, not required. Alerts are shown (two linked); the text was not read.
places.notes: Official page contact block prints Latitude 29.855409 and Longitude -97.697742. The Wikipedia infobox point 29.85528, -97.69778 agrees within a few metres. The National Weather Service URL on the page was not used. County Caldwell and acreage 453 are from the Wikipedia infobox (the official page gives neither). Camping per the official page: sites with water and electricity or full hookups, group sites, and a group recreation hall. The page mentions camping under the tall trees along the creek bank but does not label tent sites, so tent is not coded. Dark Sky: not on the TPWD dark skies page and not stated by Wikipedia. Nearby names are from the official page; distances not checked.

places.name: Old Tunnel State Park
places.coord_point: park address and contact block (10619 Old San Antonio Road, Fredericksburg TX 78624)
nearby: Lyndon B. Johnson State Park & Historic Site
places.blurb: A 16-acre Hill Country park known for its bat viewing, with no camping; advance tickets are needed after 5 p.m. in season.
places.status_note: Camping is not allowed. From May 1 to Oct. 31, a bat-viewing ticket bought in advance is required to remain in the park after 5 p.m.; tickets are not sold on site, and ranger programs also need tickets. The trail is open year-round from sunrise to 5 p.m. Alerts are shown (a screwworm notice); the text was not read.
places.notes: COUNTY CONFLICT: Wikipedia's infobox says Kendall County and a directory agrees, but one adventure-travel listing places the park in Gillespie County. The official mailing address is Fredericksburg, the Gillespie County seat, and the Wikipedia lead says the park sits halfway between Fredericksburg and Comfort. Kendall is coded because the infobox and the directory agree; please check against a county GIS layer before printing. Official page contact block prints Latitude 30.101079 and Longitude -98.820704; the Wikipedia point 30.101, -98.821 agrees. The reservations URL is the bat-viewing ticket link, not a campsite booking, and the official page's tracking parameter was dropped. Acreage 16.1 is from the Wikipedia infobox. Dark Sky: stargazing is mentioned as an activity only, and the TPWD dark skies page does not list the park.

places.name: Sea Rim State Park
places.coord_point: park contact block (19335 S. Gulfway Drive, Sabine Pass TX 77655)
nearby: Sabine Pass Battleground State Historic Site
places.blurb: Gulf marsh park with 15 campsites with utilities, one lodging cabin, primitive beach camping and horse sites.
places.status_note: No closure or day-use-only notice. Reservations recommended for camping and day use, not required. Alerts are shown; the text was not read.
places.notes: COORDINATE DISAGREEMENT: the official contact block (29.676156, -94.044008) and the Wikipedia infobox point (29.69939, -94.02545) are about 3.2 km apart, over the 2 km limit. The official point was used. Acreage: Wikipedia's infobox total area is 4,141 acres, used here; the official page says 4,000 acres of marshlands (a description, not a total). County Jefferson and nearest city Port Arthur (Wikipedia infobox); the park's own address city is Sabine Pass, used as nearest_town. Camping per the official page: 15 campsites with utilities (coded as rv_hookups, which is the closest kind on the list), one lodging cabin, primitive camping on the beach at West Beach with no facilities, and horse sites. Dark Sky: not on the TPWD dark skies page and not stated by Wikipedia. Nearby names are from the official page and the Wikipedia article; distances not checked.

places.name: Chamizal National Memorial
places.coord_point: memorial point from Wikipedia infobox; the NPS page prints no coordinates. Mailing address on the NPS page: 800 South San Marcial Street, El Paso TX 79905
places.blurb: A 55-acre El Paso memorial, a unit of the National Park Service since 1974.
places.status_note: Visitor-center hours and any alert text were not confirmed: the NPS page did not print hours, and its Alerts link was not followed.
places.notes: Coordinates are the Wikipedia infobox point only; the NPS page prints none, so this is a second-hand point and should be checked against a map before it is printed. County El Paso is inferred from the city address and the Wikipedia category tag (protected areas of El Paso County); the infobox does not state a county. Acreage 54.90 is from the Wikipedia infobox. Establishment February 4, 1974 is from Wikipedia. The Wikipedia article is long (130,670 characters); only the infobox and its first part were read. The NPS page gives no camping or directions details that were retrieved. Dark Sky: not on the TPWD dark skies page; not checked on darksky.org (403).

places.name: Sabine National Forest
places.coord_point: forest-wide point from the Wikipedia infobox. The Sabine Ranger District office is 5050 State Hwy 21 East, Hemphill TX 75948 (official Forest Service offices page, no coordinates printed); the office point was not geocoded
places.blurb: East Texas national forest around Toledo Bend Reservoir, with lakeside campgrounds and recreation areas.
places.status_note: The official page lists an active alert, 'Sabine National Forest-Trail Between the Lakes' (text not read). The office asks visitors to call 409-625-1940 for current trail and campground status. Office hours Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed federal holidays.
places.notes: The official forest page prints no coordinates, so the lat/lon is the Wikipedia infobox point (31.34083, -93.84222), which is near Hemphill. Whether it falls within about 2 km of the district office has not been checked. County Sabine is the Hemphill county seat. The official page names five counties: Sabine, San Augustine, Shelby, Jasper and Newton. Acreage 160,656 is the official page's printed figure (Wikipedia says 160,873). Campgrounds named on the official page: Lakeview Campground, on Toledo Bend and run by the Sabine River Authority of Texas under permit, and Red Hills Lake, which the page says offers camping and was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1940. The official page lists Boles Field as a picnic area centred on a historic fox hound cemetery; Wikipedia and a third-party guide call it a campground. Camping types were NOT confirmed for any site, so camping_kinds is left empty. The official offices page gives the phone as (409) 625-1940 or 1-833-546-9563. No reservation system link was found, so reservations_url is null. Dark Sky: not a dark sky site per the TPWD page and nothing found elsewhere.
